findings.description: The guard uses all(arg.help is not None ...) but the new docstring and the commit intent say the section is written if at least one argument is documented. When some arguments have help and others do not, the whole Positional arguments section is now suppressed.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a command with two positional arguments where only one has help text. Previously format_arguments wrote the section listing the documented argument. Now all() is False because the other argument's help is None, so the section is skipped and the documented argument disappears from the help output. The mechanism is the all() condition contradicting the docstring's 'if at least one is documented'. Impact: users running --help lose documented positional arguments silently.

findings.description: With no positional arguments, all() over an empty list returns True, so an empty 'Positional arguments' section heading is now emitted.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a command with no Argument parameters, which is common. The old code only wrote the section when args was non-empty. The new guard passes vacuously, so formatter.section is entered with no rows and the heading appears in help output for commands that take no positional arguments. Impact: a spurious empty section header in the help text of many commands.
